# Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never
  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job…

blocks.text:
# Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never
  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them
  # into ONE lcov (union DA hits, never cat — same as the core guards)
  # and runs the pinned crap4dart against flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
  # It is also the only home of the config guards: badge sync (AC1),
  # generated-exclude parity (E1) and the only-down git-history threshold
  # guard (AC3) — a raised threshold cannot merge, a new one (bootstrap)
  # can.
  app-crap-gate:
    name: Flutter app CRAP ratchet
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [changes, flutter-tests]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no app/shared changes — flutter_app CRAP green-skipped (required context reported)"
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # only-down guard diffs thresholds against the base
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - name: Pub cache (crap4dart)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}
          restore-keys: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}-
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: app-coverage-shard-*
          path: app-coverage-shards
      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          count=$(ls app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          if [ "$count" != "2" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected 2 app shard coverage reports, got $count"
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p flutter_app/coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info \
            app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info
      - name: Config guards — badge sync, exclude parity, only-down (AC1/E1/AC3)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          [ -n "$BASE_SHA" ] || BASE_SHA=HEAD~1
          python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down "$BASE_SHA"
      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: pin bumped 0.2.1 → >=0.9.5 for the gate framework.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 (analyzer 14.4 refresh).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 <0.12.0 — same bounded pin as the core job;
          # 0.11.0 carries the Type-2 duplication gate the repo pins to.
          # coverage.run_tests: false in both configs — the merged shard
          # lcov above is the source; never re-run the suite here.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
          cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json > crap_report.json

      # Issue #490 AC2: publish the ranked CRAP JSON even when the ratchet
      # is red (analyze writes the report to stdout before its non-zero
      # exit) — descents rank from this artifact, never from a local
      # ad-hoc run.
      - name: Upload crap_report.json artifact (issue 490 AC2)
        if: always() && (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: crap_report
          path: flutter_app/crap_report.json
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Pixel and flutter gates over test/golden/goldens (issue 447)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart check

  # Issue #283: fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by the test-core template — a

Hmm so cc=5 at 0% coverage → 25+5=30. CRAP 30.12 → 25(1-cov)³ + 5 = 30.12 → (1-cov)³ = 1.0048 → cov ≈ -0.16%? That's odd. Maybe the analyzer computes coverage over a slightly bigger range with average cov slightly > 0: cov = 0.1%: 25·(0.999)³+5 = 29.99. cov negative isn't possible...

Maybe formula includes rounding differently, e.g. uses block coverage percentage 0.04 → 25·(1-0.0004)... no.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1343
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1343
- **Title**: fix(1336): widget eval failures surface as error cards, not infinite spinners
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1336-widgets-uitree-false` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +449
- **Deletions**: -135
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T19:54:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T02:12:18Z

## PR Description

## Root cause

Three layers stack into the report from #1336:

1. **The runtime package swallows widget-eval failures.** `FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend.run` (js_widget_runtime @ pinned bd1e7c22) evaluates the whole app as one IIFE: `(function(){ try { <bootstrap> <widgetJs> } catch(e){ jsr.showError(...) } })()`. A **syntax error** means the IIFE never parses — the inner `catch` (and `jsr.showError`) never exists to run. `runtime.evaluate` returns an `isError` result, which the backend only `debugPrint`s (`widget eval error: …`) and then resolves normally. No throw, no render.
2. **The host treats "start resolved" as healthy.** `JsAppEngine.start()` completed, `tree` stayed null, and every surface (fullscreen view, board tile, dynamic-widget canvas) rendered its spinner forever. The runtime-level errors DO get the built-in error card (`jsr.showError`); only the parse/eval-before-first-render class was invisible.
3. **The `uiTree set: false` log line is misleading.** It prints `$_disposed` — the engine *liveness* flag, which is `false` for every *live* engine. Healthy and broken engines alike log `uiTree set: false`, which is exactly the marker in the issue title; it diagnoses nothing.

## Fix (host-side, this repo)

- `JsAppEngine`: when `start()` completes, arm a null-tree watchdog (`_watchUiTree`). If `tree` is still null after `uiTreeWarnAfter` (default **10 s**), it sets `bootError` (widget id + entry file + failure mode) and logs a first-class `WARNING` line to the apps log. The watchdog is pinned to the engine instance it armed on — a restart or dispose cancels it.
- The three surfaces render the failure instead of spinning forever:
  - **Fullscreen app view** → the existing start-error card with the message;
  - **Board tile** (`AppTileHost`) → the same icon fallback a failed boot gets (never blank, never spinner);
  - **Dynamic widget canvas** (`widget_tile.js` path) → the existing expandable error tile with retry.
- Isolation (AC2) was already structural — each widget boots its own `JsAppEngine` with its own native JS context — and is now pinned by the AC test.

Why host-side: the precise eval-error text lives in the runtime package's `evaluate` result string, unreachable at the pinned commit (bd1e7c22 `debugPrint`s it). The error card names the failure mode precisely ("produced no UI tree within 10s of engine start — the app source likely fails to parse (syntax error); fix the widget source and retry"). A follow-up in flutter_js_widget_runtime (stop swallowing `result.stringResult`, fix the `_disposed` log line) would upgrade the card with the verbatim JS error text; say the word and I'll file it.

## Verification

- AC-first test (`js_app_engine_test.dart`, native JSC bridge group): a **syntax-error** widget + a healthy neighbour. RED before the fix (the new engine surface doesn't exist — compile-stage red), GREEN after: `start()` resolves with tree still null (the exact spinner shape), the neighbour renders `neighbour-ok` untouched, and `bootError` surfaces with the widget id within the (test-shortened) warn window.
- Scoped gates (temp Flutter SDK 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 + fleet pub-cache — the system toolchain is unusable on this host, documented): `flutter analyze` on the 4 touched lib files → no issues; `flutter test` on `js_app_engine_test.dart` + `app_tile_host_test.dart` + `dynamic_widget_tile_test.dart` + `js_app_view_test.dart` → **103/103**; the full engine-booting family (js_app_* ×9, preflight, apps_store, bridge parity, launcher screen) → **124/124**; `dart format` on touched files.
- Golden disclosure: `store_screenshots_test.dart` (4 tests) and `apps_golden_test.dart` "app view start-error chrome" fail **identically with the fix stashed** — pre-existing host-side golden mismatches on this Mac, not from this change.
- Device acceptance (AC2's five named apps render on current main): the widget sources are user-installed on device (nothing is bundled in the repo anymore), so this needs a real device/simulator run — exact repro: install/sync the five apps, open the Widgets board; every tile must render or show its own error card within ~10 s of engine start (no infinite spinners). Post-merge/CI.


Fixes #1336


## Review round (eaf4ff8af)

- A render landing **after** the warn window now clears `bootError` — a slow-but-healthy widget recovers in place on every surface instead of hiding behind a permanent error card (failing-first engine test: 400 ms window, render at 1.5 s; pre-fix failed with exactly the stale-verdict symptom).
- `bootError` is a plain display `String` — no `Bad state:` prefix in cards.
- Widget tests for all three surfaces (tile icon fallback, fullscreen error card with widget id, canvas boot-error tile), all on the touched-surface suites: 126/126 green.
- `DynamicMessagesService._failNoUi` records the engine's watchdog message when it fired — one verdict, one wording, everywhere.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-06):
## Automated Code Review — APPROVE (with comments)

**Summary**: Host-side fix for gh-1336 is correct and well-guarded: the watchdog is pinned to the engine instance it armed on (restart/dispose cancel it via the `identical()` liveness check, which runs before any notifier read, with no awaits between the check and the writes), and all three surfaces (fullscreen view, board tile, dynamic canvas) now render failure states instead of infinite spinners. No blocking issues found.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ `bootError` is never cleared if the tree arrives after the 10s window — a widget whose first render lands late shows a permanent error card (one-line fix: clear it in the `onRender` callback).
- ⚠️ The three UI-surface wirings have no widget tests (only the engine-level watchdog is tested); the existing `_FakeTileEngine` harness makes this cheap to add.
- 💡 The canvas now runs two overlapping 10s no-UI watchdogs (`DynamicMessagesService._failNoUi` vs the new engine watchdog) with different error messages; `StateError` as the payload leaks a "Bad state:" prefix into user-facing cards; `js_app_view.dart` duplicates the start-error card block verbatim.

**Next Steps**:
1. Clear `bootError` when the tree arrives (`onRender: (t) { bootError.value = null; tree.value = t; }`) so a late-rendering widget recovers.
2. Add a widget test per surface for the `bootError` → error-card/icon wiring (extend `_FakeTileEngine`).
3. Optionally: converge the two no-UI watchdogs, use a `String` payload, extract the duplicated error card.

---

### Thread 7

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-07):
⚠️ Validation CI went red on the head. Guest PR: the rework agent is armed on this PR (owner directive 2026-10-04) — it fixes the findings and pushes; your own push re-runs validation just the same.

🔁 guest rework arm 1/2 (owner directive 2026-10-04)

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-06):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `bootError` is never cleared when the tree arrives after the watchdog fired**

The watchdog is one-shot: at `uiTreeWarnAfter` it checks `tree.value != null` and returns *only if the tree is already there*. If a widget's first render lands **after** the window (slow device, a bootstrap that fetches data before calling `jsr.render`, a heavy multi-file bundle), the sequence is:

1. t=10s — watchdog fires, `tree` is still null → `bootError` is set;
2. t=12s — the app renders, `tree.value` is assigned by the `onRender` callback (`js_app_engine.dart:403`);
3. All three surfaces check `bootError` **first**, so the app renders invisibly behind a permanent error card — and in the fullscreen view there is no retry affordance, so every close/reopen repeats the cycle (fresh engine → renders at 12s → error card again at 10s).

Before this PR such an app showed a spinner and then worked; after it it is permanently declared broken while actually running (JS timers, storage writes, and events all keep going). The `DynamicMessagesService._failNoUi` precedent doesn't have this gap because it *disposes* the engine, so a late render cannot arrive — the non-destructive engine watchdog needs an explicit recovery path.

Suggested fix — clear the flag when the tree arrives:

```dart
onRender: (t) {
  bootError.value = null; // a late render proves the boot was fine (gh-1336)
  tree.value = t;
},
```

This also makes the `ValueListenableBuilder<Object?>` on `bootError` meaningful in both directions and lets a late-rendering widget recover in place on every surface.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-06):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the three UI-surface changes ship without widget tests**

The new test covers the engine-level watchdog (bootError surfaced with the widget id, healthy neighbour unaffected) — good AC1/AC2/AC3 pinning. But the actual PR-visible behavior — *the surfaces render the failure instead of a spinner* — is untested in all three places:

- `app_tile_host.dart:361` — bootError → `AppIcon` fallback;
- `js_app_view.dart:807` — bootError → start-error card;
- `dynamic_widget_tile.dart:363` — bootError → `_errorTile` (with retry).

The existing harnesses make each of these a few lines:

- `app_tile_host_test.dart` already injects `_FakeTileEngine extends JsAppEngine` via `engineFactory`; a variant whose `start()` leaves `tree` null and sets `bootError.value = StateError('...')` (plus `uiTreeWarnAfter` shortened) directly asserts the icon fallback;
- `dynamic_widget_tile_test.dart` already drives the canvas with `dm.debugAdd(def, engine: engine(def), ...)` — one case with an engine whose `bootError` is set covers the new branch;
- `js_app_view_test.dart` likewise.

Without them, a future refactor that reorders the `bootError`/`tree` builders (or drops the outer listener) ships silently and reintroduces exactly the infinite-spinner bug this PR fixes.

Side nit in the new test: `JsAppEngine.uiTreeWarnAfter = ...` is mutated before the `try` block, but `env.writeFile`/constructors run between the assignment and the `try` — if any of those throws, the static leaks into the rest of the isolate. Move the assignment inside the `try` (the `finally` already restores the previous value).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-06):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the canvas now runs two overlapping no-UI watchdogs with different messages**

The engine-level watchdog (`uiTreeWarnAfter`, 10s) duplicates an existing mechanism: `DynamicMessagesService` already arms a per-widget 10s no-UI watchdog (`noUiGrace` / `_failNoUi` in `dynamic_messages.dart:108,290-335`) for exactly this failure class, which disposes the engine and records the service-level boot error.

For a dynamic-canvas widget both timers fire ~simultaneously (the engine's arms a few µs earlier inside `start()`), so the user sees:

1. the engine error tile — "widget 'x' (…) produced no UI tree within 10s …" (this PR);
2. then ~ms later the service error tile replaces it — "Widget produced no UI — the script may be invalid or empty." (`_failNoUi` disposes the engine and notifies).

Not broken (both are error tiles, no crash — the disposed engine's notifier is safely out of the tree after the rebuild), but it's double bookkeeping and the same failure shows two different messages depending on which watchdog wins the race, while tiles/fullscreen show only the new message. Consider converging: `_failNoUi` could consult `engine.bootError` (recording its text instead of the generic one) or be retired in favor of the engine-level flag once the canvas surfaces it — one watchdog, one message, everywhere.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-06):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `StateError` as the payload leaks a "Bad state:" prefix into user-facing cards**

`bootError` is rendered directly with `'$bootError'` on all three surfaces (`appsStartError('$bootError', …)` in `js_app_view.dart:807`, `_errorTile(context, '$bootError')` in `dynamic_widget_tile.dart:366`). `StateError.toString()` renders as:

```
Bad state: widget 'broken' (apps/broken/widget.js) produced no UI tree within 10s …
```

The `Bad state: ` prefix is a Dart implementation detail with no meaning for the widget author or end user reading the card. Since nothing catches/types this value (it's `ValueNotifier<Object?>` used purely as a display payload), a plain `String` carries the same information and renders cleaner:

```dart
bootError.value =
    "widget '${app.id}' ($entryFile) produced no UI tree within $waited "
    'of engine start — the app source likely fails to parse (syntax '
    'error); fix the widget source and retry';
```

If a typed error is preferred for future programmatic consumers, a small `BootError` class (or an `Exception`) avoids the prefix while keeping structure.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-06):

💡 **SUGGESTION: verbatim duplication of the start-error card**

# pr-1343: fix(1336): widget eval failures surface as error cards, not infinite spinners

## Description

## Root cause

Three layers stack into the report from #1336:

1. **The runtime package swallows widget-eval failures.** `FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend.run` (js_widget_runtime @ pinned bd1e7c22) evaluates the whole app as one IIFE: `(function(){ try { <bootstrap> <widgetJs> } catch(e){ jsr.showError(...) } })()`. A **syntax error** means the IIFE never parses — the inner `catch` (and `jsr.showError`) never exists to run. `runtime.evaluate` returns an `isError` result, which the backend only `debugPrint`s (`widget eval error: …`) and then resolves normally. No throw, no render.
2. **The host treats "start resolved" as healthy.** `JsAppEngine.start()` completed, `tree` stayed null, and every surface (fullscreen view, board tile, dynamic-widget canvas) rendered its spinner forever. The runtime-level errors DO get the built-in error card (`jsr.showError`); only the parse/eval-before-first-render class was invisible.
3. **The `uiTree set: false` log line is misleading.** It prints `$_disposed` — the engine *liveness* flag, which is `false` for every *live* engine. Healthy and broken engines alike log `uiTree set: false`, which is exactly the marker in the issue title; it diagnoses nothing.

## Fix (host-side, this repo)

- `JsAppEngine`: when `start()` completes, arm a null-tree watchdog (`_watchUiTree`). If `tree` is still null after `uiTreeWarnAfter` (default **10 s**), it sets `bootError` (widget id + entry file + failure mode) and logs a first-class `WARNING` line to the apps log. The watchdog is pinned to the engine instance it armed on — a restart or dispose cancels it.
- The three surfaces render the failure instead of spinning forever:
  - **Fullscreen app view** → the existing start-error card with the message;
  - **Board tile** (`AppTileHost`) → the same icon fallback a failed boot gets (never blank, never spinner);
  - **Dynamic widget canvas** (`widget_tile.js` path) → the existing expandable error tile with retry.
- Isolation (AC2) was already structural — each widget boots its own `JsAppEngine` with its own native JS context — and is now pinned by the AC test.

Why host-side: the precise eval-error text lives in the runtime package's `evaluate` result string, unreachable at the pinned commit (bd1e7c22 `debugPrint`s it). The error card names the failure mode precisely ("produced no UI tree within 10s of engine start — the app source likely fails to parse (syntax error); fix the widget source and retry"). A follow-up in flutter_js_widget_runtime (stop swallowing `result.stringResult`, fix the `_disposed` log line) would upgrade the card with the verbatim JS error text; say the word and I'll file it.

## Verification

- AC-first test (`js_app_engine_test.dart`, native JSC bridge group): a **syntax-error** widget + a healthy neighbour. RED before the fix (the new engine surface doesn't exist — compile-stage red), GREEN after: `start()` resolves with tree still null (the exact spinner shape), the neighbour renders `neighbour-ok` untouched, and `bootError` surfaces with the widget id within the (test-shortened) warn window.
- Scoped gates (temp Flutter SDK 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 + fleet pub-cache — the system toolchain is unusable on this host, documented): `flutter analyze` on the 4 touched lib files → no issues; `flutter test` on `js_app_engine_test.dart` + `app_tile_host_test.dart` + `dynamic_widget_tile_test.dart` + `js_app_view_test.dart` → **103/103**; the full engine-booting family (js_app_* ×9, preflight, apps_store, bridge parity, launcher screen) → **124/124**; `dart format` on touched files.
- Golden disclosure: `store_screenshots_test.dart` (4 tests) and `apps_golden_test.dart` "app view start-error chrome" fail **identically with the fix stashed** — pre-existing host-side golden mismatches on this Mac, not from this change.
- Device acceptance (AC2's five named apps render on current main): the widget sources are user-installed on device (nothing is bundled in the repo anymore), so this needs a real device/simulator run — exact repro: install/sync the five apps, open the Widgets board; every tile must render or show its own error card within ~10 s of engine start (no infinite spinners). Post-merge/CI.


Fixes #1336


## Review round (eaf4ff8af)

- A render landing **after** the warn window now clears `bootError` — a slow-but-healthy widget recovers in place on every surface instead of hiding behind a permanent error card (failing-first engine test: 400 ms window, render at 1.5 s; pre-fix failed with exactly the stale-verdict symptom).
- `bootError` is a plain display `String` — no `Bad state:` prefix in cards.
- Widget tests for all three surfaces (tile icon fallback, fullscreen error card with widget id, canvas boot-error tile), all on the touched-surface suites: 126/126 green.
- `DynamicMessagesService._failNoUi` records the engine's watchdog message when it fired — one verdict, one wording, everywhere.

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
          [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ] && stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          case " $stages " in *"flutter"*) echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"test-core"*) echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"analyze"*) echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # Issue #551: test/integration changes select the mock-LLM leg.
          case " $stages " in *"integration-mock"*) echo "intmock=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # All nine stages selected = a shared/unknown path changed:
          if [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ]; then
            # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
            stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          fi
          if [ "$(echo $stages | wc -w)" -eq 9 ]; then
            echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #303: the #262 DoD perf gate must red-block the MERGE for
          # trajectory regressions, not only the release — before #551 the
          # only integration leg outside PRs was tag-time. The perf-gate
          # leg re-selects the same gate via --tags perf. Paths = everything
          # the #262 fix touched: ledger core, fa_ui tr…

# Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never
  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them
  # into ONE lcov (union DA hits, never cat — same as the core guards)
  # and runs the pinned crap4dart against flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
  # It is also the only home of the config guards: badge sync (AC1),
  # generated-exclude parity (E1) and the only-down git-history threshold
  # guard (AC3) — a raised threshold cannot merge, a new one (bootstrap)
  # can.
  app-crap-gate:
    name: Flutter app CRAP ratchet
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [changes, flutter-tests]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no app/shared changes — flutter_app CRAP green-skipped (required context reported)"
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # only-down guard diffs thresholds against the base
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - name: Pub cache (crap4dart)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}
          restore-keys: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}-
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: app-coverage-shard-*
          path: app-coverage-shards
      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          count=$(ls app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          if [ "$count" != "2" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected 2 app shard coverage reports, got $count"
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p flutter_app/coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info \
            app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info
      - name: Config guards — badge sync, exclude parity, only-down (AC1/E1/AC3)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          [ -n "$BASE_SHA" ] || BASE_SHA=HEAD~1
          python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down "$BASE_SHA"
      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: pin bumped 0.2.1 → >=0.9.5 for the gate framework.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 (analyzer 14.4 refresh).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 <0.12.0 — same bounded pin as the core job;
          # 0.11.0 carries the Type-2 duplication gate the repo pins to.
          # coverage.run_tests: false in both configs — the merged shard
          # lcov above is the source; never re-run the suite here.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
          cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json > crap_report.json

      # Issue #490 AC2: publish the ranked CRAP JSON even when the ratchet
      # is red (analyze writes the report to stdout before its non-zero
      # exit) — descents rank from this artifact, never from a local
      # ad-hoc run.
      - name: Upload crap_report.json artifact (issue 490 AC2)
        if: always() && (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: crap_report
          path: flutter_app/crap_report.json
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Pixel and flutter gates over test/golden/goldens (issue 447)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart check

  # Issue #283: fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by the test-core template — a
  # duration-balanced manifest (scripts/faui_test_shards.json, rebalanced
  # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml), one file executed by exactly ONE shard,
  # goldens excluded exactly as before (host-locked). Shards fan out INSIDE
  # the job graph; only the aggregate Quality gate is a required check, so
  # a red shard = red gate and path-skipped = neutral (AC4 semantics). A
  # single failed matrix leg can be rerun alone via "Re-run failed jobs"
  # (E1) — the gate then re-aggregates the same results.
  test-faui:
    name: fa_ui tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 12
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:

blocks.text:
Found the root cause of the CRAP ratchet failure:

```
CRAP threshold exceeded: 30.12 > 30.0
```

The pinned threshold in `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml` is 30.0, and some function now measures 30.12 CRAP. Almost certainly `_watchUiTree` or a related new function in `js_app_engine.dart` — new code with partial coverage → CRAP = cc² × (1-cov)³ + cc... Actually CRAP formula: `crap = comp^2 * (1 - cov)^3 + comp` where cov is coverage fraction. If cc=3 and coverage ~0.x: 3²·(1-cov)³+3. For CRAP 30.12: comp=3 → 9(1-cov)³+3 = 30.12 → (1-cov)³ = 3.013 → impossible (max 9+3=12 when cov=0). comp=4: 16(1-cov)³+4 = 30.12 → (1-cov)³ = 1.6325 → 1-cov = 1.177 > 1 impossible. comp=5: 25(1-cov)³+5=30.12 → (1-cov)³=1.0048 → 1-cov ≈ 1.0016 → cov ≈ 0% (rounding). Hmm so cc=5 at 0% coverage → 25+5=30. CRAP 30.12 → 25(1-cov)³ + 5 = 30.12 → (1-cov)³ = 1.0048 → cov ≈ -0.16%? That's odd. Maybe cov is a tiny nonzero: (1-cov)³ = 1.0048 means 1-cov = 1.00159 → cov = -0.0016. Negative coverage? That can't be.

Alternative: the threshold check might use "max CRAP score" across functions where the max function has CRAP 30.12 with cc=5 and coverage 0%... that gives 30. Hmm, 30.12 could come from a different formula variant: CRAP1 = cc²·(1-cov)³ + cc; with cov=0, cc=5 → 30. 30.12 is close. Maybe the analyzer computes coverage over a slightly bigger range with average cov slightly > 0: cov = 0.1%: 25·(0.999)³+5 = 29.99. cov negative isn't possible...

Maybe formula includes rounding differently, e.g. uses block coverage percentage 0.04 → 25·(1-0.0004)... no.

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] CI -->|No| THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([All findings fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["PR Rework TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it"] R2["✅ If the existing tests only cover a single-item/simple case, add a test for the multi-item/edge case the finding points at — a fix without a test for that exact case is not verified"] R3["✅ Returned findings: your fix must differ from the previous attempt and the new/updated test must prove it"] R4["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] R5["✅ Verification order: finalize ALL fixes BEFORE launching the full test-suite/coverage run — a run over a tree you are still editing is wasted"] R6["✅ Long runs (full suite, coverage) start with bash background: true and are collected via bash_job status/output between other steps — NEVER foreground sleep-polling (see prompts/bash_tools.md)"] R7["❌ NEVER kill a running verification because files changed after it started — let it finish, treat the result as stale, re-run deliberately"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/response.md must be Markdown (# headings, - bullets, ``` code fences)"] F2["Required sections: ## Issues/Notes (if any), ## Approach, ## Files Modified, ## Test Coverage"] F3["Be surgical but thorough — fix exact issues flagged, then check same pattern across codebase"] F4["Do NOT refactor unrelated code or add unrequested features"] F5["When open PR review threads exist, create outputs/review_replies/*.md files and reference them from outputs/review_replies.json"] ``` - When `input//pr_discussions_raw.json` contains open PR review threads: - Write one Markdown file per open thread under `outputs/review_replies/`. - Write `outputs/review_replies.json` with one entry per open thread, including `inReplyToId`, `threadId`, and a `reply` field that contains the path to the matching `.md` file. - Do **not** put reply bodies inline in the JSON. ## PR Rework — Output Rules Rework posts **only** to the Pull Request. ## PR Description

## Root cause

Three layers stack into the report from #1336:

1. **The runtime package swallows widget-eval failures.** `FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend.run` (js_widget_runtime @ pinned bd1e7c22) evaluates the whole app as one IIFE: `(function(){ try { <bootstrap> <widgetJs> } catch(e){ jsr.showError(...) } })()`. A **syntax error** means the IIFE never parses — the inner `catch` (and `jsr.showError`) never exists to run. `runtime.evaluate` returns an `isError` result, which the backend only `debugPrint`s (`widget eval error: …`) and then resolves normally. No throw, no render.
2. **The host treats "start resolved" as healthy.** `JsAppEngine.start()` completed, `tree` stayed null, and every surface (fullscreen view, board tile, dynamic-widget canvas) rendered its spinner forever. The runtime-level errors DO get the built-in error card (`jsr.showError`); only the parse/eval-before-first-render class was invisible.
3. **The `uiTree set: false` log line is misleading.** It prints `$_disposed` — the engine *liveness* flag, which is `false` for every *live* engine. Healthy and broken engines alike log `uiTree set: false`, which is exactly the marker in the issue title; it diagnoses nothing.

## Fix (host-side, this repo)

- `JsAppEngine`: when `start()` completes, arm a null-tree watchdog (`_watchUiTree`). If `tree` is still null after `uiTreeWarnAfter` (default **10 s**), it sets `bootError` (widget id + entry file + failure mode) and logs a first-class `WARNING` line to the apps log. The watchdog is pinned to the engine instance it armed on — a restart or dispose cancels it.
- The three surfaces render the failure instead of spinning forever:
  - **Fullscreen app view** → the existing start-error card with the message;
  - **Board tile** (`AppTileHost`) → the same icon fallback a failed boot gets (never blank, never spinner);
  - **Dynamic widget canvas** (`widget_tile.js` path) → the existing expandable error tile with retry.
- Isolation (AC2) was already structural — each widget boots its own `JsAppEngine` with its own native JS context — and is now pinned by the AC test.

Why host-side: the precise eval-error text lives in the runtime package's `evaluate` result string, unreachable at the pinned commit (bd1e7c22 `debugPrint`s it). The error card names the failure mode precisely ("produced no UI tree within 10s of engine start — the app source likely fails to parse (syntax error); fix the widget source and retry"). A follow-up in flutter_js_widget_runtime (stop swallowing `result.stringResult`, fix the `_disposed` log line) would upgrade the card with the verbatim JS error text; say the word and I'll file it.

## Verification

- AC-first test (`js_app_engine_test.dart`, native JSC bridge group): a **syntax-error** widget + a healthy neighbour. RED before the fix (the new engine surface doesn't exist — compile-stage red), GREEN after: `start()` resolves with tree still null (the exact spinner shape), the neighbour renders `neighbour-ok` untouched, and `bootError` surfaces with the widget id within the (test-shortened) warn window.

# pr-1343: fix(1336): widget eval failures surface as error cards, not infinite spinners

## Description

## Root cause

Three layers stack into the report from #1336:

1. **The runtime package swallows widget-eval failures.** `FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend.run` (js_widget_runtime @ pinned bd1e7c22) evaluates the whole app as one IIFE: `(function(){ try { <bootstrap> <widgetJs> } catch(e){ jsr.showError(...) } })()`. A **syntax error** means the IIFE never parses — the inner `catch` (and `jsr.showError`) never exists to run. `runtime.evaluate` returns an `isError` result, which the backend only `debugPrint`s (`widget eval error: …`) and then resolves normally. No throw, no render.
2. **The host treats "start resolved" as healthy.** `JsAppEngine.start()` completed, `tree` stayed null, and every surface (fullscreen view, board tile, dynamic-widget canvas) rendered its spinner forever. The runtime-level errors DO get the built-in error card (`jsr.showError`); only the parse/eval-before-first-render class was invisible.
3. **The `uiTree set: false` log line is misleading.** It prints `$_disposed` — the engine *liveness* flag, which is `false` for every *live* engine. Healthy and broken engines alike log `uiTree set: false`, which is exactly the marker in the issue title; it diagnoses nothing.

## Fix (host-side, this repo)

- `JsAppEngine`: when `start()` completes, arm a null-tree watchdog (`_watchUiTree`). If `tree` is still null after `uiTreeWarnAfter` (default **10 s**), it sets `bootError` (widget id + entry file + failure mode) and logs a first-class `WARNING` line to the apps log. The watchdog is pinned to the engine instance it armed on — a restart or dispose cancels it.
- The three surfaces render the failure instead of spinning forever:
  - **Fullscreen app view** → the existing start-error card with the message;

blocks.text:
# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
          [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ] && stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          case " $stages " in *"flutter"*) echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"test-core"*) echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"analyze"*) echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # Issue #551: test/integration changes select the mock-LLM leg.
          case " $stages " in *"integration-mock"*) echo "intmock=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # All nine stages selected = a shared/unknown path changed:
          if [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ]; then
            # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
            stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          fi
          if [ "$(echo $stages | wc -w)" -eq 9 ]; then
            echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #303: the #262 DoD perf gate must red-block the MERGE for
          # trajectory regressions, not only the release — before #551 the
          # only integration leg outside PRs was tag-time. The perf-gate
          # leg re-selects the same gate via --tags perf. Paths = everything
          # the #262 fix touched: ledger core, fa_ui tr…

# Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never
  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job…

blocks.text:
# Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never
  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them
  # into ONE lcov (union DA hits, never cat — same as the core guards)
  # and runs the pinned crap4dart against flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
  # It is also the only home of the config guards: badge sync (AC1),
  # generated-exclude parity (E1) and the only-down git-history threshold
  # guard (AC3) — a raised threshold cannot merge, a new one (bootstrap)
  # can.
  app-crap-gate:
    name: Flutter app CRAP ratchet
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [changes, flutter-tests]
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no app/shared changes — flutter_app CRAP green-skipped (required context reported)"
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # only-down guard diffs thresholds against the base
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - name: Pub cache (crap4dart)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}
          restore-keys: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}-
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: app-coverage-shard-*
          path: app-coverage-shards
      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          count=$(ls app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          if [ "$count" != "2" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected 2 app shard coverage reports, got $count"
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p flutter_app/coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info \
            app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info
      - name: Config guards — badge sync, exclude parity, only-down (AC1/E1/AC3)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          [ -n "$BASE_SHA" ] || BASE_SHA=HEAD~1
          python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down "$BASE_SHA"
      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: pin bumped 0.2.1 → >=0.9.5 for the gate framework.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 (analyzer 14.4 refresh).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 <0.12.0 — same bounded pin as the core job;
          # 0.11.0 carries the Type-2 duplication gate the repo pins to.
          # coverage.run_tests: false in both configs — the merged shard

blocks.text:
Found the root cause of the CRAP ratchet failure:

```
CRAP threshold exceeded: 30.12 > 30.0
```

The pinned threshold in `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml` is 30.0, and some function now measures 30.12 CRAP. Almost certainly `_watchUiTree` or a related new function in `js_app_engine.dart` — new code with partial coverage → CRAP = cc² × (1-cov)³ + cc... Actually CRAP formula: `crap = comp^2 * (1 - cov)^3 + comp` where cov is coverage fraction. If cc=3 and coverage ~0.x: 3²·(1-cov)³+3. For CRAP 30.12: comp=3 → 9(1-cov)³+3 = 30.12 → (1-cov)³ = 3.013 → impossible (max 9+3=12 when cov=0). comp=4: 16(1-cov)³+4 = 30.12 → (1-cov)³ = 1.6325 → 1-cov = 1.177 > 1 impossible. comp=5: 25(1-cov)³+5=30.12 → (1-cov)³=1.0048 → 1-cov ≈ 1.0016 → cov ≈ 0% (rounding). Hmm so cc=5 at 0% coverage → 25+5=30. CRAP 30.12 → 25(1-cov)³ + 5 = 30.12 → (1-cov)³ = 1.0048 → cov ≈ -0.16%? That's odd. Maybe cov is a tiny nonzero: (1-cov)³ = 1.0048 means 1-cov = 1.00159 → cov = -0.0016. Negative coverage? That can't be.

Alternative: the threshold check might use "max CRAP score" across functions where the max function has CRAP 30.12 with cc=5 and coverage 0%... that gives 30. Hmm, 30.12 could come from a different formula variant: CRAP1 = cc²·(1-cov)³ + cc; with cov=0, cc=5 → 30. 30.12 is close. Maybe the analyzer computes coverage over a slightly bigger range with average cov slightly > 0: cov = 0.1%: 25·(0.999)³+5 = 29.99. cov negative isn't possible...

Maybe formula includes rounding differently, e.g. uses block coverage percentage 0.04 → 25·(1-0.0004)... no.

Let me not guess; download the crap_report.json artifact to see the offender. The artifact ID 11456940495 was uploaded. `gh run download` or `gh api`.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1343
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1343
- **Title**: fix(1336): widget eval failures surface as error cards, not infinite spinners
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1336-widgets-uitree-false` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +449
- **Deletions**: -135
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T19:54:20Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T02:12:18Z

## PR Description

## Root cause

Three layers stack into the report from #1336:

1. **The runtime package swallows widget-eval failures.** `FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend.run` (js_widget_runtime @ pinned bd1e7c22) evaluates the whole app as one IIFE: `(function(){ try { <bootstrap> <widgetJs> } catch(e){ jsr.showError(...) } })()`. A **syntax error** means the IIFE never parses — the inner `catch` (and `jsr.showError`) never exists to run. `runtime.evaluate` returns an `isError` result, which the backend only `debugPrint`s (`widget eval error: …`) and then resolves normally. No throw, no render.
2. **The host treats "start resolved" as healthy.** `JsAppEngine.start()` completed, `tree` stayed null, and every surface (fullscreen view, board tile, dynamic-widget canvas) rendered its spinner forever. The runtime-level errors DO get the built-in error card (`jsr.showError`); only the parse/eval-before-first-render class was invisible.
3. **The `uiTree set: false` log line is misleading.** It prints `$_disposed` — the engine *liveness* flag, which is `false` for every *live* engine. Healthy and broken engines alike log `uiTree set: false`, which is exactly the marker in the issue title; it diagnoses nothing.

## Fix (host-side, this repo)

- `JsAppEngine`: when `start()` completes, arm a null-tree watchdog (`_watchUiTree`). If `tree` is still null after `uiTreeWarnAfter` (default **10 s**), it sets `bootError` (widget id + entry file + failure mode) and logs a first-class `WARNING` line to the apps log. The watchdog is pinned to the engine instance it armed on — a restart or dispose cancels it.
- The three surfaces render the failure instead of spinning forever:
  - **Fullscreen app view** → the existing start-error card with the message;
  - **Board tile** (`AppTileHost`) → the same icon fallback a failed boot gets (never blank, never spinner);
  - **Dynamic widget canvas** (`widget_tile.js` path) → the existing expandable error tile with retry.
- Isolation (AC2) was already structural — each widget boots its own `JsAppEngine` with its own native JS context — and is now pinned by the AC test.

Why host-side: the precise eval-error text lives in the runtime package's `evaluate` result string, unreachable at the pinned commit (bd1e7c22 `debugPrint`s it). The error card names the failure mode precisely ("produced no UI tree within 10s of engine start — the app source likely fails to parse (syntax error); fix the widget source and retry"). A follow-up in flutter_js_widget_runtime (stop swallowing `result.stringResult`, fix the `_disposed` log line) would upgrade the card with the verbatim JS error text; say the word and I'll file it.

## Verification

- AC-first test (`js_app_engine_test.dart`, native JSC bridge group): a **syntax-error** widget + a healthy neighbour. RED before the fix (the new engine surface doesn't exist — compile-stage red), GREEN after: `start()` resolves with tree still null (the exact spinner shape), the neighbour renders `neighbour-ok` untouched, and `bootError` surfaces with the widget id within the (test-shortened) warn window.
- Scoped gates (temp Flutter SDK 3.47.5 / Dart 3.13.4 + fleet pub-cache — the system toolchain is unusable on this host, documented): `flutter analyze` on the 4 touched lib files → no issues; `flutter test` on `js_app_engine_test.dart` + `app_tile_host_test.dart` + `dynamic_widget_tile_test.dart` + `js_app_view_test.dart` → **103/103**; the full engine-booting family (js_app_* ×9, preflight, apps_store, bridge parity, launcher screen) → **124/124**; `dart format` on touched files.
- Golden disclosure: `store_screenshots_test.dart` (4 tests) and `apps_golden_test.dart` "app view start-error chrome" fail **identically with the fix stashed** — pre-existing host-side golden mismatches on this Mac, not from this change.
- Device acceptance (AC2's five named apps render on current main): the widget sources are user-installed on device (nothing is bundled in the repo anymore), so this needs a real device/simulator run — exact repro: install/sync the five apps, open the Widgets board; every tile must render or show its own error card within ~10 s of engine start (no infinite spinners). Post-merge/CI.


Fixes #1336


## Review round (eaf4ff8af)

- A render landing **after** the warn window now clears `bootError` — a slow-but-healthy widget recovers in place on every surface instead of hiding behind a permanent error card (failing-first engine test: 400 ms window, render at 1.5 s; pre-fix failed with exactly the stale-verdict symptom).
- `bootError` is a plain display `String` — no `Bad state:` prefix in cards.
- Widget tests for all three surfaces (tile icon fallback, fullscreen error card with widget id, canvas boot-error tile), all on the touched-surface suites: 126/126 green.
- `DynamicMessagesService._failNoUi` records the engine's watchdog message when it fired — one verdict, one wording, everywhere.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-06):
## Automated Code Review — APPROVE (with comments)

**Summary**: Host-side fix for gh-1336 is correct and well-guarded: the watchdog is pinned to the engine instance it armed on (restart/dispose cancel it via the `identical()` liveness check, which runs before any notifier read, with no awaits between the check and the writes), and all three surfaces (fullscreen view, board tile, dynamic canvas) now render failure states instead of infinite spinners. No blocking issues found.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ `bootError` is never cleared if the tree arrives after the 10s window — a widget whose first render lands late shows a permanent error card (one-line fix: clear it in the `onRender` callback).
- ⚠️ The three UI-surface wirings have no widget tests (only the engine-level watchdog is tested); the existing `_FakeTileEngine` harness makes this cheap to add.
- 💡 The canvas now runs two overlapping 10s no-UI watchdogs (`DynamicMessagesService._failNoUi` vs the new engine watchdog) with different error messages; `StateError` as the payload leaks a "Bad state:" prefix into user-facing cards; `js_app_view.dart` duplicates the start-error card block verbatim.

**Next Steps**:
1. Clear `bootError` when the tree arrives (`onRender: (t) { bootError.value = null; tree.value = t; }`) so a late-rendering widget recovers.
2. Add a widget test per surface for the `bootError` → error-card/icon wiring (extend `_FakeTileEngine`).
3. Optionally: converge the two no-UI watchdogs, use a `String` payload, extract the duplicated error card.

---

### Thread 7

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-07):
⚠️ Validation CI went red on the head. Guest PR: the rework agent is armed on this PR (owner directive 2026-10-04) — it fixes the findings and pushes; your own push re-runs validation just the same.

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-06):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `bootError` is never cleared when the tree arrives after the watchdog fired**

The watchdog is one-shot: at `uiTreeWarnAfter` it checks `tree.value != null` and returns *only if the tree is already there*. If a widget's first render lands **after** the window (slow device, a bootstrap that fetches data before calling `jsr.render`, a heavy multi-file bundle), the sequence is:

1. t=10s — watchdog fires, `tree` is still null → `bootError` is set;
2. t=12s — the app renders, `tree.value` is assigned by the `onRender` callback (`js_app_engine.dart:403`);
3. All three surfaces check `bootError` **first**, so the app renders invisibly behind a permanent error card — and in the fullscreen view there is no retry affordance, so every close/reopen repeats the cycle (fresh engine → renders at 12s → error card again at 10s).

Before this PR such an app showed a spinner and then worked; after it it is permanently declared broken while actually running (JS timers, storage writes, and events all keep going). The `DynamicMessagesService._failNoUi` precedent doesn't have this gap because it *disposes* the engine, so a late render cannot arrive — the non-destructive engine watchdog needs an explicit recovery path.

Suggested fix — clear the flag when the tree arrives:

```dart
onRender: (t) {
  bootError.value = null; // a late render proves the boot was fine (gh-1336)
  tree.value = t;
},
```

This also makes the `ValueListenableBuilder<Object?>` on `bootError` meaningful in both directions and lets a late-rendering widget recover in place on every surface.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-06):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the three UI-surface changes ship without widget tests**

The new test covers the engine-level watchdog (bootError surfaced with the widget id, healthy neighbour unaffected) — good AC1/AC2/AC3 pinning. But the actual PR-visible behavior — *the surfaces render the failure instead of a spinner* — is untested in all three places:

- `app_tile_host.dart:361` — bootError → `AppIcon` fallback;
- `js_app_view.dart:807` — bootError → start-error card;
- `dynamic_widget_tile.dart:363` — bootError → `_errorTile` (with retry).

The existing harnesses make each of these a few lines:

- `app_tile_host_test.dart` already injects `_FakeTileEngine extends JsAppEngine` via `engineFactory`; a variant whose `start()` leaves `tree` null and sets `bootError.value = StateError('...')` (plus `uiTreeWarnAfter` shortened) directly asserts the icon fallback;
- `dynamic_widget_tile_test.dart` already drives the canvas with `dm.debugAdd(def, engine: engine(def), ...)` — one case with an engine whose `bootError` is set covers the new branch;
